item.title: Graphiti vs Hindsight: Agent Memory Compared (November 2026)
item.description:
Short answer: pick Hindsight if you want a finished memory server under MIT that you can run with one Docker command, with no graph database to run beside it. Pick Graphiti if you are building a temporal knowledge graph into your own system and you want to control the graph database, the prompts and the service yourself.

Graphiti is a library, not a service. Its author says it is “self-hosted only” and that you “operate the graph database, retrieval, and surrounding service yourself”. Hindsight is a memory server you run or use as a hosted API. Graphiti facts come from its README and repository (github.com/getzep/graphiti, read 27 November 2026). Hindsight facts come from its README, benchmarks site and pricing page.

item.title: Knowledge Graphs for AI Agent Memory: How They Work
item.description:
A knowledge graph memory stores what an AI agent learns as entities (a user, a company, a product) connected by relationships (“works at”, “prefers”, “reported bug in”). An LLM extracts those entities and relationships from conversations and documents, and the agent later retrieves facts by searching the graph and following its links. The graph makes connections and changes explicit, which flat vector memory can’t do.

This page explains how graph memory is built, how retrieval works, the main tools (Graphiti, Neo4j Agent Memory, Cognee, Hindsight, GraphRAG), and when a graph beats a vector store. For the GitHub stars and client downloads of the graph databases these tools run on (Neo4j, FalkorDB, Kuzu and others), see graph database statistics.

item.title: Zep vs Mem0: Temporal Graph vs Fact Memory
item.description: Zep vs Mem0 is a choice between two ways of storing what an agent learns. Zep keeps a temporal knowledge graph where every fact has a validity window, so old facts are invalidated rather than lost. Mem0 extracts short facts into a vector store with entity linking, and ranks them by semantic, keyword and entity match. Mem0 is open source; Zep is a managed service with Graphiti as its open-source core.

item.title: What Is Zep Memory? Zep Cloud, Graphiti and Pricing
item.description:
Zep memory is Zep Cloud, a managed service that stores what an agent learns from users and data in a temporal context graph, then returns a prompt-ready block of relevant facts. Its open-source core is Graphiti, a framework for knowledge graphs that track when facts change. The old self-hosted Zep Community Edition is deprecated.

This page covers what Zep is now, how Zep memory stores and retrieves data, the Zep paper, pricing, self-hosting, and integrations. Sources are Zep’s docs, the Graphiti repo and the Zep pricing page.

item.title: Temporal Reasoning in AI Memory: Time-Aware Recall
item.description:
Temporal reasoning in AI memory is the ability to answer questions that depend on time: what happened first, how long ago, what was true in March, what changed since. Most memory systems search by meaning, which is blind to time. Getting it right takes timestamps, relative dates resolved at write time, and time-range filters.

It’s one of the weakest areas for current systems, and benchmarks test it directly. This page explains why time breaks memory, the kinds of temporal questions agents face, and the techniques that measurably help. The broader design of memory systems is covered in AI agent memory explained.
